title: Epsilon-soft Monte Carlo control
brief: Learn action values from your own epsilon-greedy episodes on a small grid, and see that the policy you learn is the best epsilon-soft policy, not the optimal one.
hints: The epsilon-greedy row is np.full(A, epsilon / A) with 1 - epsilon added at the first argmax. The rows must sum to one.
epsilon_soft_world mixes each action's outcome with the average over actions: (1 - epsilon) * P + epsilon * P.mean(axis=1, keepdims=True), and the same for R.
In mc_control, break ties among best actions at random with rng.choice(np.flatnonzero(Q[s] == Q[s].max())). With Q = 0 everywhere, argmax always picks action 0 and walks into the top wall.
Update each first-visited (s, a) pair once per episode: Q[s, a] += alpha * (G[t] - Q[s, a]).
